result:
Editing the reason phrase in the web UI now sends `reason`, and the backend now accepts `reason`, so the edit reaches the response. I didn't run the Python tests or the frontend tests, per your instructions.

The old code had the frontend sending `{ response: { msg } }`. The PUT handler in `app.py` then ran `setattr(response, "msg", ...)`, which set a plain attribute on the response object. The real `reason` was never changed.

- **`web/src/js/components/FlowView/HttpMessages.tsx`**: the reason editor now dispatches `{ response: { reason } }`.
- **`mitmproxy/tools/web/app.py`**: the update handler accepts `reason` (and `http_version`) instead of `msg`. `msg` is no longer accepted and now returns a 400 "Unknown update response.msg". Any API client that sends `msg` will hit that.
- **`test/mitmproxy/tools/web/test_app.py`**: the update test sends `reason`. I only changed the key, so the test doesn't yet assert that `f.response.reason` changed.
